summary: Defines a MIME directory profile for holding an LDAP schema. This lets schema definitions be carried as a MIME content type.

eli5.summary: It defines a way to put the rulebook of a directory into an email-style attachment.

questions: mime directory profile for ldap schema
how to carry ldap schema as mime
exchange ldap schema as email attachment
subtitle: A way to package LDAP schema definitions as email attachments.

tldr.problem: LDAP schema definitions are complex and difficult to send over email or store as standalone documents. There is no standard format for exchanging schema between systems.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a MIME directory profile called schema-ldap-0 that packages LDAP schema definitions (object classes, attribute types, matching rules, and syntaxes) as a text/directory MIME content type that can be sent in email or carried in other systems.
tldr.outcome: Schema definitions can now be exchanged as email attachments or in other MIME contexts, enabling the Internet schema listing service to accept and distribute schema definitions using standard email infrastructure.

today: RFC 2927 is an Informational RFC from 2000. It enabled email-based exchange of LDAP schema definitions. Today, schema is typically managed within LDAP servers or distributed through configuration management systems, but this profile remains useful for schema interchange and documentation purposes.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
An LDAP schema consists of object class definitions (what kinds of entries can exist), attribute type definitions (what fields are available), matching rule definitions (how to compare values), and syntax definitions (how values are encoded).

Typically, schema definitions are embedded in LDAP servers or distributed as server configuration files. This RFC defines how to represent a complete LDAP schema using the MIME directory format (a text-based encoding also used for vCards and calendars).
sections.eli5: A directory rulebook needs a standard way to be packaged and sent.

sections.title: The schema-ldap-0 MIME Directory Profile
sections.content:
The profile name is schema-ldap-0. It defines several types used to represent schema elements: ldapSchemas (the schema container), objectClasses (object class definitions), attributeTypes (attribute definitions), matchingRules (comparison rules), matchingRuleUse (matching rule relationships), and ldapSyntaxes (value syntaxes).

The ldapSchemas type is the core element that describes the schema itself, including which other schemas it imports and which elements it defines. Only one ldapSchemas value is allowed per content (though later versions might allow multiple).

The charset parameter MUST be UTF-8 to ensure schema values can be used directly in LDAP without translation.
sections.eli5: The profile lists what kind of things (classes, attributes, rules) appear in the message.

sections.title: MIME Directory Types
sections.content:
The RFC registers six new MIME directory types. The ldapSchemas type contains a schema definition including a numeric OID that uniquely identifies the schema, optional human-readable names, and lists of what elements are defined or imported.

attributeTypes defines individual LDAP attribute types, specifying their OID, name, syntax, and matching rules. objectClasses defines object classes (what kinds of entries can exist), listing which attributes they must have and which are optional. matchingRules defines comparison rules. matchingRuleUse shows which attributes use which matching rules. ldapSyntaxes defines the encoding of values.

All types except ldapSchemas can be multivalued, appearing multiple times in the same message.
sections.eli5: Each type represents a different kind of schema rule that needs to be communicated.

sections.title: Example
sections.content:
A simple example shows how a schema with two object classes (top and thing) and two attributes (objectClass and name) is represented. The message begins with ldapSchemas declaring the schema OID and the object classes and attributes it defines. Then individual attributeTypes lines give the full definition of each attribute, and objectClasses lines define the classes. Finally, ldapSyntaxes defines the syntaxes for the string and OID types.

Note that schema definitions can be long and may contain embedded line breaks, so implementors must handle content lines longer than 76 bytes and use content transfer encodings when needed.
sections.eli5: The example shows the real format of a small schema in the message.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: A MIME body part containing a schema-ldap-0 profile can be part of a digitally signed MIME message. When the signer is certified by a trusted third party, it is possible to verify both that the schema has not been modified in transit and that it comes from a trusted source.
sections.eli5: The schema can be digitally signed to prove it has not been changed.
